html:
Primož Trubar was a Protestant preacher, born in 1508 at Rašica in central Slovenia, who wrote the first printed books in the Slovene language.

A Catholic priest won over to the Reformation, he had to flee Ljubljana for Germany. In 1550 he published a Catechism and an Abecedarium in Slovene at Tübingen, the start of Slovene literature. He went on to translate the New Testament and write some twenty more books. His follower Jurij Dalmatin translated the whole Bible in 1584. The Counter Reformation wiped out Slovene Protestantism, but the written language survived. Trubar is a national figure in Slovenia, and his portrait was on the one euro coin.
